thread:
Marcos: Heads-up — ACME APAC asking for Redwood Dedicated commit sizing. Key constraints: big tail bursts during APAC market hours, hard egress caps from their cloud partner in ap-southeast-1, and a strict monthly commit for SLA. They want guidance: how to set committed throughput vs expected burst, and how to avoid nasty billing surprises?
Alex: Quick thoughts — size baseline for steady-state (95th pct of 5m windows) and add a separate burst allowance. Don’t over-index to absolute peak.
Alex: Rule of thumb I use: commit_baseline ~= ceil(peak_95th * safety_factor) where safety_factor=1.1-1.3 depending on SLA. Convert to GPU-mins with tokens/request * avg_latency.
Priya: +1. Also split by region: APAC committed floor + cross-region burst fallback (eu-west as second line). APAC egress limits mean sometimes we should prefer local model variants (quantized) to reduce bandwidth.
Priya: Proposal: phase commits over 3 months: month1 60% baseline, month2 80%, month3 full. Use canary routes for 10% traffic to test quantized variant.
Jen: Watch network egress billing. APAC egress + inter-region fallback can blow cost. If they have per-GPU egress caps, we might need to surface that in the contract: "burst overage billing applies when egress > X GB/day".
billing-bot: Auto-check — based on provided demo trace (120M tokens/month, 35% burst within trading hours), projected monthly overage with no burst contract: ~$4,200. With a 20% burst bucket added to commit, projected overage reduces to ~$900. Link: https://billing/redwood/projects/ACME-APAC/estimates
capacity-bot: APAC pool snapshot: headroom ~120 A100-eq GPU-mins/day; fragmentation 14% (small allocations + pinned instances). Nearby region eu-west-1 headroom ~420 GPU-mins/day.
Marcos: Noted. Concern: even if we commit a baseline, fragmentation means we might not get contiguous capacity during spikes. Any ops mitigations?
Alex: We can reserve a small dedicated burst pool pinned to the customer's commit (hot spare) — reduces fragmentation risk. Oper cost increases but predictable.
Alex: Example config I’d propose to include in the commit addendum:
```
commit:
  baseline_tps: 800
  burst_bucket_tps: 200
  region_primary: ap-southeast-1
  fallback_region: eu-west-1
  phase_months: 3
  hot_spare: true
```
Marcos: @Priya can you own the phase-in plan and coordinate network egress thresholds with billing?
Priya: I’ll take it. I’ll run two sims: (A) baseline-only commit, (B) baseline + 20% burst pool + hot spare. Will post cost/availability deltas tomorrow.
Jen: FYI: legal wants a clause clarifying cross-region failover can incur additional egress charges if traffic flows out of region. Add that to the contract checklist.
billing-bot: Reminder: when committing, we should include a reconcile window (30d) for actual usage vs committed throughput to avoid invoice disputes.
Marcos: Sounds good. Quick action items: 1) Priya run sims, 2) Alex draft commit config + hot-spare ops playbook, 3) Jen update contract checklist with egress language, 4) Ops: confirm APAC fragmentation remediation options.
capacity-bot: Noted. If hot_spare=true we can reduce fragmentation by reserving 2x GPU-groups, estimated impact: headroom drop to ~90 GPU-mins/day but contiguous allocation increases by ~48%.
Marcos: Thanks all — let’s sync tomorrow 09:00 PDT. :calendar:
Alex: Adding a short checklist to the thread later with the few numbers we need from ACME (p90 qps, avg tokens/request, retention of model variants).
Priya: ping me if you need the sim inputs.
Jen: I’ll draft the contract lines and share for review.
Marcos: Closing loop — tagging this for the Dedicated commit holder doc once we finalize. :thumbsup:
